scenes.headline: How a decision model scores options instead of writing
scenes.sub: Command Code's Agr, read from its weights and code.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Arlo! This model answers typed questions with a probability for every option, and never writes a word.

scenes.text: Every question is a branch off one shared state, and the answer is the base model's own output layer, read at one position.
scenes.mark: the base model's own output layer
scenes.say: Every question hangs off one shared state, and the answer is read from the base model's own output layer.

steps.say: The state goes in once. Each question follows, its options listed under single letters.
The whole request is one forward pass.
At the end of each question, only that question's letter scores are kept.
Divide by a fitted temperature, take a softmax, and every option has a probability. Nothing is sampled.

steps.label: plain sequence
steps.say: In a plain sequence, a later question would read the earlier ones.

steps.label: the shared state
steps.say: Instead, every question reads the whole state.

steps.label: its own block only
steps.say: And inside its own block, only itself. Each answer is as if it were asked alone.

parts.note: logits of the option letters, soft-capped
parts.say: z is the logit of each option letter.

parts.note: fitted on development data by log loss
parts.say: T of n is a temperature set by the number of options, fitted by log loss.

scenes.title: Same output layer, before and after

left.title: Stock weights
left.say: Read the untrained base model this way, and a yes or no answer must be divided by almost nine.

right.title: After the fine-tune
right.say: After the fine-tune, the same output layer needs about one point two.

scenes.title: Decision Index, Tools area
scenes.say: Overall, the fine-tune adds under a point, and a third of a point on tools, where others already score higher.

scenes.text: A decision model reads answers from the output layer it already had; training teaches the hidden state to land well-scaled logits there.
scenes.say: The answer comes from the output layer the model already had. Training teaches the hidden state to land well scaled scores there.

recap: One pass, a branch per question
Letter logits, then a fitted temperature
Self-run score, measure on your data
scenes.say: One pass, a branch per question, letter scores and a fitted temperature. And a self-run score, so measure on your own data.
